root_idea.summary: The root has two lexically distinct orientations: filling or bringing something to capacity, and moving away or creating distance; enmity is understood as a form of separation.
root_idea.development: The filling branch yields loading a vessel and the passive participle meaning laden. The distancing branch yields driving away, going far, and enmity. The sources also associate filling or gathering with preparedness, such as readiness to weep.

qac_form_accounting.reason: A Quran-attested passive participle with an established classical citation form and a supported Quranic meaning.

senses.usage_conditions: In all three Quranic occurrences, it describes a ship or vessel filled, loaded, and equipped.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill or load a ship, house, chamber, or similar space; also, to fill a town with horsemen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may also be used intransitively of what is in a ship when it fills the ship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drive away, remove, or pursue a person or group; an intensely acid thing is said to drive away flies.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be a people, party, or individual; the expression concerning acid is figurative lexical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To run vehemently or go far; of dogs, to go far in pursuit without catching prey.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The dog usage is a specialized description of prolonged pursuit without securing game.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bear rancor, malice, or spite toward someone, or to show enmity toward him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The first construction is explicitly used with عَلَيْهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To appoint someone to the office of a شِحْنَة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This usage is reported in postclassical works.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To treat one another with rancor, malice, or enmity; to exchange reviling, blame, or reproach without reaching combat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two derived forms express reciprocal treatment; the reproach usage is described as falling short of fighting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sheath a sword; also, in a contrary usage, to draw the sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Both opposite meanings are explicitly reported for the same verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be ready or about to weep; for the eyes to water as weeping approaches.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction describes imminent weeping or its physical onset without restricting the subject to a particular age or gender.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prepare oneself to shoot someone or to shoot at someone with an arrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with بِسَهْمٍ to specify preparation for shooting with an arrow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The contents or load of a ship sufficient to fill it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The vocalization is reported with some uncertainty in the source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A body of men sufficient to guard, control, or hold a province or city; a troop of horsemen posted in a country or town.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term refers to an organized guarding or controlling force, not merely to a commander.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The quantity of fodder allotted to beasts as sufficient for a day and a night.
Rancor, malice, spite, vehement hatred, or enmity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It is used of enmity existing between people.
In the cited poetic passage, the preferred interpretation is as a plural referring to shiploads, while its morphological analysis is disputed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dog that goes far in pursuit without catching prey or game.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized nominal description of a pursuing dog.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who bears enmity, rancor, or spite toward another.
Becoming angered or being made angry.
A rancorous enemy; in transmitted usage, a schismatic religious innovator or transgressor, or one who harbors rancor toward the Companions of the Prophet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Transmitted interpretations also include one who abandons the institutes or customary rule of his prophet, speaks against his people, or sheds their blood.

cautions: The analysis of شُحُون as a ship-load term is accompanied by a reported morphological dispute; the preferred lexical interpretation is retained with that qualification.
The Form IV sword usage is explicitly contronymous: the same reported form can mean either sheathing or drawing the sword.
